---
title: Command Line Interface (CLI)
---

The `sib` command creates keys, enrolls them, signs instructions, verifies files and decodes
blocks. With a dev key it runs in dev mode and every command that signs or verifies prints the
dev-mode warning to standard error; with a passkey enrolled it signs through the browser and
verifies in enforced mode.

All commands read `SIB_HOME` for the directory that holds keys and the registry (default:
`~/.sib`).

Inside the repository, run it as `uv run sib`. After `source .venv/bin/activate`, or after
`uv tool install --editable .`, plain `sib` works; the examples below use the plain form.


## Basic Usage

```bash
# Create a dev key and enroll it for a signer
sib keygen --signer alice@example.com --enroll

# Or enroll a passkey (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a security key) through the browser
sib enroll --signer alice@example.com

# Sign an instruction given on the command line, writing the block to stdout
sib sign --signer alice@example.com --expires 2h --audience acme/dev-agent \
  --text "You may deploy the current main branch to staging whenever the test suite passes."

# Sign the contents of a file instead
sib sign --signer alice@example.com --expires 2h --audience acme/dev-agent --file instruction.txt

# Verify every block in a file for a given audience
sib verify CLAUDE.md --audience acme/dev-agent

# Decode blocks without verifying them
sib inspect CLAUDE.md
```


## Commands

### keygen

Create a dev-mode Ed25519 key under `$SIB_HOME/dev-keys/` and optionally enroll it. Give
`--signer`, `--kid`, or both.

`--signer ID`
: The signer the key belongs to. When `--kid` is omitted the key identifier is derived as
  `<signer>#dev-<year>-<month>` (e.g., `alice@example.com#dev-2026-09`).

`--kid ID`
: Key identifier, by convention `signer#label`. Overrides the derived name.

`--enroll`
: Also add the public key to the registry. Requires `--signer`.

`--dev`
: Accepted for clarity; dev mode is the only mode `keygen` supports.

### enroll

Enroll a passkey through the browser, or add a public key given on the command line. Without
`--public-key` the command starts the local signing app, opens the enroll page and waits for the
authenticator; see [Biometric Signing](../components/signing.qmd#enrollment).

`--signer ID`
: The signer the key belongs to. Required.

`--kid ID`
: Key identifier. Derived as `<signer>#passkey-<id>` for a passkey; required with
  `--public-key`.

`--public-key B64URL`
: Enroll this raw public key, base64url encoded, instead of a passkey.

`--alg ALG`
: Signature algorithm of `--public-key` (default: `EdDSA`).

`--dev`
: Mark the key as a dev-mode key. Without it the key is enrolled as `enforced`.

`--timeout SECONDS`
: How long to wait for the browser (default: 180).

`--no-browser`
: Print the page URL instead of opening a browser.

`--browser NAME`
: The browser to open the page in, when the system default lacks passkey support or a password
  manager in it captures the prompt: a name the Python `webbrowser` module knows (`safari`,
  `chrome`, `firefox`) or a command the URL is appended to (`'open -a Safari'`). Defaults to
  `SIB_BROWSER`, then the system default.

### sign

Clearsign an instruction. The command prints the canonical text and the terms before signing, so
what you see is what you sign. With a passkey it opens the sign page and waits for the
authenticator; with a dev key it signs at once.

Either identifier is enough: a `--kid` names its signer through the registry, and a `--signer`
with exactly one enrolled key names that key. A signer's passkeys are preferred over their dev
keys; with several candidates, the command lists them and asks for `--kid`.

`--signer ID`
: The signer, written to the `iss` header field. Derived from `--kid` when omitted; checked for
  agreement when both are given.

`--kid ID`
: The key to sign with. Derived from `--signer` when the signer has one candidate key.

`--expires DURATION`
: Validity window from now, as `30m`, `2h` or `1d` (default: `2h`).

`--audience ID`
: The deployment or harness the block is for. Optional for a dev key; required for a passkey,
  because a block with no audience is refused in enforced mode.

`--canon RULE`
: Canonicalization rule (default: `text/1`). See [Canonicalization](../components/canonicalization.qmd).

`--text TEXT`
: The instruction, given directly. Line structure does not matter under `text/1`.

`--file PATH`
: File holding the instruction, or `-` for standard input (default when `--text` is absent).

`--out PATH`
: Write the block to a file instead of standard output.

`--dev`
: Sign with a dev key even when a passkey is enrolled; refuses a `--kid` that is not a dev key.

`--timeout SECONDS`, `--no-browser`, `--browser NAME`
: As for `enroll`.

### install

Install the SIB hooks into an agent harness. Takes the harness as a positional argument;
`claude-code` is the only one implemented.

`--settings-json FILE`
: Write one settings file carrying the hooks and the autoMode rule, for `claude --settings FILE`.
  The recommended path: both halves stay together and apply only to runs that name the file.

`--project PATH`
: Merge the hook entries into `PATH/.claude/settings.json` and print the autoMode rule to add to
  `~/.claude/settings.json` by hand, since Claude Code does not read `autoMode` from project
  settings.

`--layers LIST`
: Comma-separated subset of `prompt`, `pre` and `post` (default: all three). Use it to run the
  classifier note without the PreToolUse gate, or the gate alone.

`--no-prose`
: Omit the autoMode rule.

`--print-auto-mode`
: Print the autoMode block as JSON and nothing else.

The hook entries record the Python interpreter that ran the installer, so run it from the
environment that has `sib` installed. See [Claude Code](../integration/claude-code.qmd) for what
each hook does.

### verify

Extract and verify every block in a file. Exits with status 0 only when at least one block was
found and every block verified. The mode is enforced once a passkey is enrolled in the registry
and dev before that, unless `SIB_MODE` or a flag says otherwise.

`FILE`
: The file to check, or `-` for standard input.

`--audience ID`
: The audience of this harness; blocks for another audience fail with `audience_mismatch`.

`--enforced`
: Verify in enforced mode: dev-mode blocks and keys confer nothing.

`--dev`
: Verify in dev mode: both kinds of key verify, with the warning.

`--json`
: Print the provenance manifest as JSON instead of the human-readable summary.

### inspect

Decode every block in a file without verifying: the text as written, the clear metadata lines,
the decoded header and the first characters of the signature.

`FILE`
: The file to decode, or `-` for standard input.


## Exit Codes

`sib verify` returns 0 when every block verified, 1 otherwise, including when no block was
found. `sib sign` returns 1 and writes no block when the authenticator's assertion does not
verify, naming the status. The other commands return 0 on success and exit with a message on a
usage error, such as signing with a key that is not enrolled for the signer.


## Environment

`SIB_HOME`
: Directory for dev keys and `registry.json` (default: `~/.sib`).

`SIB_MODE`
: `dev` or `enforced`; overrides the default described under `verify`.

`SIB_BROWSER`, `SIB_WEBAUTHN_PORT`, `SIB_REQUIRE_ATTESTATION`, `SIB_ATTESTATION_ROOTS`
: Passkey enrollment and signing; see [Biometric Signing](../components/signing.qmd#environment).
